solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He cuts end off ponytail for party

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for the haircutter is dropped

parts.note: a man who cuts hair for a living is a barber
cue is an old spelling of queue, a pigtail or tail of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser snips the tip off someone's ponytail, getting them ready for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end off' removes the R from BARBER, leaving BARBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is an outdoor party where food is grilled over charcoal.

clue.text: Start to yawn, following one way to show lack of interest

indicators.note: the yawn letter comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: one is the indefinite article a
a path is a way or track

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Starting to yawn is one way to show you're bored.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, a want of feeling or concern about anything.

clue.text: Vessel hugging port in swell

indicators.note: the boat word wraps itself around the port letter

parts.note: a boat is a vessel on water
port is the left side of a ship, abbreviated L

explanation.surface: A ship rides the swell close to harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour but is the left side, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloat is to swell up or puff out, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bird seen in seed containers by part of yard

parts.note: chaff is the husks that encase grain seeds
an inch is a fraction of a yard, 1/36 of it

explanation.surface: A bird spotted pecking at seed holders by a section of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yard' suggests a garden, but it is the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch with a pinkish breast.

clue.text: Note I spelt out?

parts.note: E is a note of the musical scale

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a message they wrote down counts as a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I SPELT into PISTLE, after E. The whole clue also describes the answer: a note spelt out is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, a written note spelt out at length.

clue.text: After a short time, present something trifling

indicators.note: the present-time word follows the short-time abbreviation

parts.note: min is the abbreviation for minute, a short time
now means the present moment

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a little gift after a short delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but means the current time.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a tiny fish, figuratively an insignificant person or thing.

clue.text: Woman swinging both ways

definitions.note: a polite title for a woman, and its letters read alike in both directions

indicators.note: a word that swings both ways reads the same in either direction

parts.note: a polite title for a woman, and its letters read alike in both directions

explanation.surface: A woman described as bisexual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging both ways' sounds like sexuality but means the word reads the same backwards and forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a woman, or a brothel keeper.

clue.text: Garments wreathing around

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Clothes wrapped round and round something like a wreath.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is clothing worn in bed, such as pyjamas and nightdresses.

clue.text: Stuffed, I've room to eat end of chicken — I'm not a fussy eater

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the chicken letter, as though eating it
stuffed means messed up, so these letters are reordered
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A diner who is full still has space for the last of the chicken, being unfussy about food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffed' rearranges I'VE ROOM into OMIVORE; 'to eat' puts N, the end of chicken, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats both plants and meat, so is not selective about diet.

clue.text: Turn a rogue monkey out of Eastern temple

indicators.note: turn means the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: a dog is a scoundrel or rogue

indicators.note: the compass letter is taken out of the monkey word

parts.note: an ape is a monkey in loose usage
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An instruction to expel a wicked monkey from an Asian shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops E from APE, leaving AP; 'Turn' reverses A DOG AP. 'Eastern' does double duty: the E removed and part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a temple in East Asia.

clue.text: Poor cut-off country chap

indicators.note: the country's last letter is cut off

parts.note: India is a country
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: A poor man from an isolated nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-off' removes the final A of INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy, lacking the means to live.

clue.text: Picture of soup's suitable

parts.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup
to fit, as in 'cut to fit', means suitable or apt

explanation.surface: A judgment on whether a picture of soup is fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A photofit is a composite likeness of a suspect, a picture assembled from witness memory.

clue.text: Test one has as a driver

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK vehicle roadworthiness test
one has is I've, I standing for one and 've for has

explanation.surface: A car's annual test has a certain function for a motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness check for cars. 'driver' looks like a motorist but means an impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is what drives someone to act, the force behind a deed.

clue.text: They'll stick up for ass hanging round yard for ages

indicators.note: the ears phrase surrounds the yard letter

parts.note: the parts that stick up on a donkey are its ears

explanation.surface: Someone loyally defends a fool who loiters in the yard, seemingly forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick up for' tempts as 'defend', but here it means literally project upwards, as a donkey's ears do.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey's years is a British idiom for a very long time.

clue.text: Set up system for measuring piece of music to help identification

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: SI is the international system of units
a song is a piece of music
aid means help

explanation.surface: Arranging a metric scheme for a musical piece to aid identification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reverses SI SONG AID to give DIAG-NOS-IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is the identification of a disease or problem from symptoms.

clue.text: Greasy liquid that'll help open troublesome door?

definitions.text: Greasy liquid that'll help open troublesome door?

parts.words: Greasy liquid that'll help open troublesome door?
parts.note: a cooking fat made from a seed; Ali Baba's cave door opened to the words 'Open Sesame'

explanation.surface: Oiling a sticky door to get it open.
explanation.walkthrough: Lubricating a stiff door suggests any oil; the joke is the magic password from Ali Baba.
explanation.definitionFit: This cooking oil is pressed from sesame seeds, the seed named in the magic password.

clue.text: Empower board member advising remotely from home

parts.note: to arm is to equip or empower
the chair presides over a board

explanation.surface: A company director given authority to advise while working from home.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic or adviser comments from comfort without first-hand experience.

clue.text: Test for driver of high-speed train, about to turn back after money cut

indicators.note: the train name comes after the trimmed money word
the last letter of the slang money word is cut

parts.note: bread is slang for money
Thalys is a high-speed train service linking Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam

indicators.note: the word for about is turned back to front

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A sobriety check for a bullet-train driver, concerning a reversal after a pay cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops D from BREAD; 'to turn back' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathalyser measures the alcohol in a motorist's breath.

clue.text: Scientist may use this hair of the dog?

definitions.meaning: a white protective coat worn in laboratories
the coat of a Labrador, read as two words

explanation.surface: A boffin reaches for a drink to cure a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair of the dog' is a hangover drink; here a Labrador's fur.
explanation.definitionFit: A white overall protects researchers in laboratories, and a Labrador's fur is its coat.

clue.text: No doubt graduate's got to eat in

indicators.note: the eating verb goes in the graduate letters

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
to etch is to eat away, as acid does

explanation.surface: A graduate certainly has to eat at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Betcha is casual speech for 'I bet you', meaning surely or without doubt.

clue.text: Dollar and some change for perfumes

parts.note: S stands in for the dollar sign
cents are coins, small change

explanation.surface: Paying for fragrances with a dollar and loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Scents are perfumes, pleasant smells worn on the skin.

clue.text: Nutty chicken perhaps brooded forever

parts.note: a hen that broods sits on eggs, so brooded is sat
ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A crazy hen kept sitting on its eggs endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty' suggests mad, but describes a peanut sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is skewered grilled meat, often chicken, served with peanut sauce.

clue.text: Pour drink over insect

indicators.note: the drink is spread over and around the insect

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink
a moth is a winged insect

explanation.surface: Tipping a drink over a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mother is a British idiom for pouring the tea for everyone.

clue.text: Head down in formal rows

indicators.note: in a down entry the head letter is moved down to the bottom

parts.note: stiff means formal, unrelaxed

explanation.surface: Bowing one's head in stiff ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffs are minor quarrels or squabbles.

clue.text: Cornish runner has argument, going up to high do?

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall; rivers run
a set-to is a fight or argument

explanation.surface: A Cornish athlete quarrels on the way to a smart party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England. 'do' is a party but also the note doh.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the singing register used to reach notes above a man's normal range.

clue.text: Business having abandoned diamonds

parts.note: off means called off, abandoned
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A firm that has given up dealing in jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a place of business or a firm's workplace.

clue.text: Bid to suppress beginnings of unresolved sexual tension, being faithful

indicators.note: the attempt word holds down the initials inside it

parts.note: a bid is an attempt, a try

indicators.note: the beginnings of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An attempt to stifle the early stirrings of romantic tension while staying loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unresolved sexual tension' is the TV-romance phrase often shortened to UST, so its initials come naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty means reliable and loyal, able to be trusted.

clue.text: In capitalism, a niche is what may secure fortune

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A market niche is the key to making money under capitalism.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a charm believed to bring good luck.
